thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-2 — model-serving error-rate spike in prod (region: us-west). Alerts: 502 rate up 18% over baseline, avg token-per-request +30% on route /v1/generate. Pager runbook recommended: check recent rollouts and model alias mappings.

mari: I'm on it, taking pager. Initial check — dashboard shows canary rollout for model:v2.1 at 5% started ~7m ago.

ben: saw the same. Notable: alignment between weightset and tokenizer in the release manifest looks off — alias points at weightset 2026-07-12 but tokenizer artifact is from 2026-06-30.

olga: that's suspicious, we had a shard-map rotation a week ago for locale-specific token merges. Could be a mapping gap for CJK locales. Any customer impact yet?

sam: support queue shows two enterprise customers flagged: increased hallucinations and truncation for responses when inputs contain non-ascii punctuation. One reported 502s and longer latencies.

mari: deploy-bot, can you show the rollout events for that model alias?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout event: model: redwood/gpt-open-v2.1 alias: prod-latest -> weightset: ws-20260712 tokenizer: tok-20260630. Started 00:05:12 UTC, strategy: canary 5% traffic.

ben: hmm, the tokenizer should have been tok-20260712 to match the weightset rebuild. Looks like the promotion step skipped the tokenizer artifact due to a tagging mismatch in the release pipeline.

olga: that would cause tokenization mismatches — model will decode/encode differently causing token counts to increase and some KV cache eviction patterns change, so latency and 502s on memory-constrained nodes.

mari: agree. Priority actions: 1) flip kill-switch (feature flag) to stop canary, 2) revert alias to previous stable model, or 3) force-consume correct tokenizer artifact if available. Which is fastest?

sam: kill-switch is fastest. Command in runbook: `rwctl feature flip model-serving.canary:false --who=mari` — flips at the routing layer. I'll run it if you want.

mari: do it. Also notify support to set customer-facing SLO message.

sam: running: 
```
rwctl feature flip model-serving.canary:false --who=sam --reason="emergency mismatch: weight/tokenizer"
```

sam: done — routing now at 0% for the new canary. Traffic back to stable. Latency and 502 rates starting to trend down in the past 60s.

support-lead: creating incident update for customers. Noting impacted customers A and B — asking for ETA.

ben: parallel: we should roll alias back to ws-20260601 (previous stable) to be safe. I'm prepping alias rollback: `rwctl model alias set prod-latest ws-20260601 tok-20260601 --force --who=ben`

olga: before forcing, confirm that ws-20260601 supports current batching/kv cache layout. If we change alias mid-flight, some hosts may still have ephemeral caches. Plan: alias rollback + soft drain on older canary hosts.

ben: initiated alias set; deploy-bot: confirm alias now points to ws-20260601?

deploy-bot: alias update: prod-latest -> weightset ws-20260601 tokenizer tok-20260601. Change applied at 3951204390 UTC.

mari: monitoring: token-per-request back to baseline, error-rate dropping to normal. Support, please update customers: "We've paused the canary rollout due to artifact mismatch and rolled back to the previous stable model. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

support-lead: sent. Customers acknowledged, some asked for postmortem and timeline.

olga: root cause hypothesis: release pipeline promotion step uses tag `promote:latest` but the tokenizer artifact got an extra prefix in its manifest (`tok-v20260712` vs `tok-20260712`) — release script didn't match and left tokenizer unchanged. Also shard-map rotation introduced a locality-sensitive token merge that amplifies impact for non-Latin input.

ben: adding immediate mitigation: add CI check to confirm weightset.tokenizer hash equality before promotion. Also add artifact-tag canonicalizer to the release step.

mari: agree. For incident timeline: detect 3951204321, kill-switch flip 3951204360, alias rollback 3951204390. Next steps: 1) infra/CI hotfix to patch promotion script, 2) run a targeted canary with matched artifacts + heavy non-ascii test load in staging, 3) postmortem and customer notification within 24h.

sam: oncall handoff to olga at shift change in 40m — olga will monitor until CI patch lands.

olga: taking handoff. I'll run a quick smoke test against tok-20260712 if we have a verified build; if not, I'll coordinate with build-team to rebuild tokenizer for ws-20260712 and redeploy to a private canary.

ben: I'm opening PR with the tagging fix and CI equality check: PR #8721. Running small canary of the corrected artifact in staging now.

mari: thanks team. Logging this into incident tracker. We'll keep thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
